critique:
field green_container, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Keep the field as described, with one addition about how the chain is run: the three color chains (green, red, blue) are run jointly as a one-to-one assignment, frame to frame. In each frame every container gets exactly one color, so no two color fields may end on the same container and no moving container may be left unassigned. When the two nearest candidates for one color are nearly tied (a few pixels apart in displacement), the tie is broken by the assignment that leaves a distinct container for the other colors with the smallest total displacement. A step whose last frame shows the containers in the same arrangement as the previous step's last frame is NOT evidence that nothing moved: when any intermediate frame shows containers displaced, the chain is still run through every frame and usually ends with two colors swapped. Example: carried green [100, 166], first frame container at [101, 168], then [110, 178], [125, 182], [130, 163], last frame [130, 160]; write [130, 160] even though the goal names only blue. e.g. [130, 160]

field red_container, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Same addition as green_container: chained jointly with the other two colors as a one-to-one assignment per frame, near-ties resolved by consistency with the other chains, every color re-chained at any step whose frames show a container displaced, even when the start and end layouts of the step look identical and even when red is not named in the goal. e.g. [101, 152]

field green_container, POLICY PROMPT
  Situation: at the decision step after the second press, while the two non-goal containers had circled each other during the press, the policy re-chained only the goal color and copied the other two fields unchanged, so one non-goal field still held a position where a different container now stood; at another step the start and end layouts of the step were identical and a near-tie between two candidates in a middle frame made the single-color chain ambiguous. This breaks PREDICTABILITY: the recorded values were the jointly chained ones. Change the instruction to a mandatory procedure placed before the worked example: (a) at every step whose frames show containers, rewrite ALL THREE fields green_container, red_container and blue_container, not only the goal color; (b) if any frame shows a container displaced from its position in the previous frame by more than a few pixels, run the chain for all three colors through every frame as a ONE-TO-ONE ASSIGNMENT: in each frame each container is assigned to exactly one color, so two fields can never end on the same container, and a container that one color leaves must be taken up by another color; (c) when the nearest candidate for one color is a near-tie (displacements within a few pixels of each other), choose the assignment that also gives the other colors a distinct nearest container with the smallest total displacement; (d) an identical container layout in the first and last frames of a step does not mean nothing moved; if middle frames show displacement, the result is usually a swap of two colors, and the chain decides which; (e) consistency check before writing: the three written values must be three different containers of the last frame, and if the goal color's field moved to a new container, the field that carried that container's old position must have moved too. Example: carried green [100, 166] and blue [130, 162]; frames show [101, 168] gliding to [110, 178], [125, 182], [130, 163], [130, 160] while the other glides from [130, 162] to [121, 151], [106, 147], [102, 165], [101, 168]; write green_container=[130, 160] and blue_container=[101, 168]. e.g. [130, 160]

field red_container, POLICY PROMPT
  Same change as green_container: rewritten at every step showing containers, chained jointly with green and blue as a one-to-one assignment per frame, near-ties broken by consistency with the other chains, identical start/end layouts still chained, and the three written values must be three distinct last-frame containers. Example: carried red [112, 194] passes [121, 184], [119, 162] (chosen over [95, 182] because blue's chain takes that one), [103, 153], last frame [101, 152]; write [101, 152]. e.g. [101, 152]

field blue_container, POLICY PROMPT
  Same change as green_container: rewritten at every step showing containers, chained jointly with green and red as a one-to-one assignment per frame, near-ties broken by consistency with the other chains, identical start/end layouts still chained, and the three written values must be three distinct last-frame containers. Example: carried blue [101, 152] passes [95, 163], [95, 182], [112, 194], last frame [114, 195]; write [114, 195]. e.g. [114, 195]
